To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The network delta is an appropriate measure of the sensitivity of the network's value to changes in the default probability of a given firm; and (2) the network delta is a good proxy for the systemic risk of a financial network.

(a) network value sensitivities are a natural extension of the classical structural risk model; (b) network Greeks can be computed efficiently using Monte-Carlo simulation; (c) the network $\Delta$, which is the first derivative of the network value with respect to a change in the default threshold, can be used as a quantitative measure for systemic risk.
